evidence.note: Installed boto3 locally and ran a real boto3 client against the running service exercising core operations: create bucket / put / get / list / presigned / copy — genuine SigV4 round-trip verification, not just assuming code works.

Ran targeted edge-case tests via boto3/requests: multipart completion including 5 MiB part-size rule and final ETag, versioning/delete markers, range GETs, anonymous bucket-policy GET, admin tenant/key creation and audit. Findings drove patches (list_object_versions, lifecycle parsing, failed-admin audit).

Added and verified a conditional PUT If-Match check, then reset /app/data for a clean grader state — iterative verify-then-patch loop, though tests were one-off scripts rather than a persistent harness.
Confirmed console only at the API level (login endpoint works); no browser/DOM/testid interaction test of visible console side-effects, which the console is actually graded on.
No concurrency/load test (the 30-client no-5xx/no-corruption requirement) appears anywhere; verification stops at single-threaded functional checks.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it ran the actual boto3 client against core operations and a substantial set of edge behaviors (multipart ETag/part-size, versioning/delete markers, ranges, presigned query-auth, conditional PUT, cross-tenant/anonymous policy, admin+audit), using results to drive fixes. But it falls short of the level-8 anchor: there is no concurrency/corruption load test, no console side-effects driven through the DOM/testids (only API-level login was checked), and the checks were sequential ad hoc scripts rather than a repeatable milestone-gating harness. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.
